rows.abstract: Under this proposed measure, NOT IMMEDIATE ARREST shall be made on any Filipino citizen, residing in his own country, before a final dtermination that such citizen is extraditable. If extradition is ganted, no articles found in possession of the accused who has been arrested may be seized provided that such articles are alleged to have intimate relation to or are the products of the crime or crimes for which the accused is sought to be extradited and there is reasonable ground to believe this to be true.

rows.abstract: Republic Act 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, is hereby amended by adding Article XXI which provides for the position of a TOURISM OFFICER in every province, city and municipality. The Tourism Officer shall: (1) formulatemesures to ensure the delivery of services and the provision of adequate facilities for tourism development and promotion; (2) conduct studies, researchers, and training programs necessary to evolve plans and programs for implementation; (3) integrate and coordinate all tourism development plans and studies; and (4) develop tourism plans and strategies and implement the same.

rows.abstract: "Corporate Reform Act of 2002." This bill seeks to regulate corporate abuses by providing among others: (1) Banning of accounting firms from providing most consulting services to companies they are auditing; (2) No registered public accounting firmshall provide audit services to an issuer if the lead audit partner or the audit partner responsible for reviewing audit, has performed audit services for that issuer in each of five (5) previous fiscal years of that issuer; (3) Prohibits any issuerto extend or maintain credit, in a form of a personal loan to or for any director or executive officer of publicly listed companies; and (4) Destruction, alteration, or falsification of records in investigations and bankruptcy is punishable with up tto 20 years.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A JOINT LEGISLATIVE-EXE CUTIVE TAX COMMISSION, DEFINING ITS OBJECTIVES, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to establish a Joint Legislative-Exe cutive Tax Commission (JLETC) that shall be tasked to undertake a comprehensive study of the need for additional revenue for accelerated national development, conduct research on taxation for thepurpose of improving the country's tax system and tax policy and recommend reforms or revisions as may be necessary to improve revenue collection and administration.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL HOMELOTS DISTRIBUTION PROGRAM
rows.abstract: "Comprehensive National Homelots Distribution Act of 2002." The lands covered by this Act shall be distributed to residents of the barangay where the land is located belonging to the lower income classes. Priority shall be given to landless and underprivileged residents who are already occupying said lot for two or more years.> The Housing and Urban Development Coordinating Council (HUDCC) shall formulate financing program to assist the beneficiaries acquire their homelots and build affordablehouses. It shall consider existing programs and develop other financing schemes in coordination with the Home Guarantee Corporation and other government financial institutions to fast track the distribution of homelots and acquisition of affordable hhousing for the beneficiaries.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06115

rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING A HEAVIER PENALTY AGAINST PUBLIC OFFICERS CHARGED WITH THE CUSTODY OF PRISONERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 223 AND 224 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: This bill punishes any public officer who shall consent to the escape of a prisoner in his custody or charge: (1) BY THE SANE PENALTY IMPOSED UPON THE FUGITIVE if the fugitive shall have been sentenced by final judgment to any penalty. (2) BY A PENALTY LOWER THAN ONE DEGREE TO THE MAXIMUM PENALTY IMPOSABLE upon the fugitive in case the fugitive shall not have been finally convicted but only held as a detention prisoner for any crime or violation of law or municipal ordinance.> If evasion of theprisoner shall have taken place through the negligence of the officer charged with conveyance or custody of the escaping prisoner; said officer SHALL SUFFER THE PENALTY LOWER THAN ONE DEGREE TO THE PENALTY IMPOSED UPON THE ESCAPEE.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06419

rows.author: D078
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 36 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8189, ENTITLED 'AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A GENERAL REGISTRATION OF VOTERS, ADOPTING A SYSTEM OF CONTINUING REGISTRATION, PRESCRIBING THE PROCEDURES THEREOF AND AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES'
rows.abstract: This bill aims to adopt a validation system for the registration of voters in order to preserve the integrity of the permanent list of voters. It mandates all registered voters to appear before the Election Registration Board of the City of Municipality where they are registered for validation of their registration within the period and in the manner prescribed by the Commission. The failure of any registered voter to appear for validation shall result in the annulment of his/her registration and shall constitute a waiver of his/her right to vote without prejudice to the application of section 8 of RA 8189.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2002-10-24

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT UPGRADING THE SALARY GRADE LEVEL OF THE SCHOOLS DISTRICT SUPERVISORS FROM SALARY GRADE NINETEEN (19) TO SALARY GRADE TWENTY-FOUR (24)
rows.abstract: Presently, the District Supervisor's Salary Grade is nineteen (SG 19) while the Salary Grade of a Secondary School Principal is 21 (SG 21). It is obvious that the Schools District Supervisors are being discriminated against by receiving a salary lower than that of what is being received by the School Principals which are under the supervision of the former. > This bill seeks to correct this anomaly by upgrading the Salary Grade of Schools District Supervisors from Salary Grade Nineteen (SG 19)to Salary Grade Twenty-Four (24).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2002-10-14

rows.author: D005
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENSURING A HIGHER STANDARD OF PROTECTION AND PROMOTION OF THE WELFARE OF MIGRANT WORKERS BY AMENDING THE FIFTH PARAGRAPH OF SECTION 10 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8042, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `MIGRANT WORKERS AND OVERSEAS FILIPINOS ACT OF 1995'
rows.abstract: It is the intention of this bill to establish a higher standard of protection and promotion of the welfare of migrant workers and Filipinos in distress. Under the fifth paragraph of Section 10 of RA 8042, an overseas worker who has been terminated from employment without just, valid or authorized cause as defined by law or contract shall be entitled to the full reimbursement of his placement fee with interest at twelve percent (12%) per annum, plus his salaries for the unexpired portion of hisemployment contract or for three months for every year of the unexpired term, whichever is less. In order to give higher standard of protection and promotion of the welfare of the migrant worker, the phrase "whichever is less" should be changed to "wwhichever is higher."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2002-10-14
